title: Shared State with Arc and Mutex
goal: Share mutable data safely across multiple threads.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Shared State

sections.text: Shared references `&T` cannot cross threads if `T` uses non-atomic reference counting. To share owned data between threads, use `Arc<T>`.

sections.caption: Arc::clone increments the atomic count without copying the vector.

sections.text: `Arc` only gives shared, read-only references. To modify shared data, wrap the inner value in a `Mutex<T>`.

sections.caption: Arc manages shared ownership, while Mutex provides interior mutability.

sections.text: Calling `lock()` on a `Mutex` blocks until the lock is acquired, returning a `MutexGuard`. The lock releases automatically when the guard goes out of scope.

sections.caption: lock() returns a Result to handle poisoned locks if another thread panicked.

explanation: Share mutable data safely across multiple threads.
